A1.evidence: Sec. III.A-F and IV: no train/test split for the in-distribution results (Table 6) is stated; Algorithm 4 only names client Dm_tr/Dm_val; zero-day protocol holds out attack classes (Sec. III.F, Table 5).

A2.evidence: Sec. III.D: per-record input 'xi = [xi_net || xi_sys]' to fully connected encoders; no windows or sequences.

A3.evidence: Sec. III.B / Algorithm 1: Z-score 'µj ← Mean(D[fj]); σj ← Std(D[fj])' and OneHotEncode(D) computed on the full dataset D before partitioning (Sec. III.C: 'the preprocessed dataset D̃ is partitioned across M logical clients').

A4.evidence: Rounds T stated (Table 5: T = 200 or 100); local epochs E appear only as a symbol in Algorithm 4 ('rounds T; local epochs E'), no value given.

A5.evidence: Sec. III.E: six configurations 'varying client count, heterogeneity level, training rounds, and aggregation strategy'; no statement that FedAvg/FedProx/Centralized used the same rounds/epochs.

A6.evidence: Table 6: Centralized, FedAvg, FedProx results per Exp1-Exp6 from authors' experiments; Table 11 related-work 'Findings' is a qualitative literature table, not a baseline comparison.

A7.evidence: Sec. IV: 'using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Macro-F1, AUC, CATS, and robustness ratio R'; no MCC/balanced accuracy/G-mean.

A8.evidence: Sec. III.C / Table 2: Dirichlet label allocation 'pm ∼ Dir(α)', α ∈ {1.0, 0.5, 0.1} with 5/10/20 clients.

A9.evidence: Detection results (Tables 6-9) are single values without dispersion; only convergence/timing (Fig. 7, Table 10) 'reported as mean ± standard deviation over five independent runs.'

A10.evidence: Zero-day protocol (Sec. III.F) holds out attack classes of the same TON_IoT dataset ('Atest = A \ Atrain'); no other dataset or capture used.

A11.evidence: No code link in the paper.
